newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money eases slightly to 3.10 pct.
newsitem.headline: German call money eases slightly to 3.10 pct.

text.p: German call money rates traded slightly softer on Monday at 3.10 percent in calm conditions.
The bulk of trades was conducted at 3.10 percent compared with Friday's range of 3.10/3.125 percent, dealers said, adding that monthly reserve holdings at the Bundesbank still looked comfortable.

"Reserve holdings can't be bad, after all there was very little interest in obtaining funds late Friday afternoon," a dealer said. For the next several sessions, dealers predicted rates would remain at current levels.
As the Bundesbank has kept its main money market rate, the repo, steady at three percent since August, dealers see little chance of rates moving much below the 3.10 percent level.
"Some really brave people may attempt to push rates down, but whether they will be successful will depend on where they are calling from," said one dealer.

On Friday banks held 41.1 billion marks in reserve at the Bundesbank, down from 42.1 billion marks held on Thursday. Meanwhile holdings for the month slipped to 42.0 billion marks from 42.8 billion marks.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average was set at 3.12633 percent on Monday after 3.13433 percent on Friday.
